oneliner.t: First-term Democratic congressman from Mobile and former Justice Department and Obama White House official, seeking re-election in a 2nd District redrawn to the 2023 Legislature map (39.9% Black voting-age population).

born.note: Single secondary source for the date. The House bio says he was raised and educated in Alabama but gives no birthplace.

upbringing.t: Son of the late Michael Figures, a civil rights lawyer and state senator who represented Beulah Mae Donald in the suit over her son's 1981 lynching (a $7 million verdict that reportedly bankrupted the United Klans of America), and of Vivian Davis Figures, who succeeded her husband in the state Senate. He attended Council Elementary, Phillips Middle and LeFlore Magnet High in Mobile, then the University of Alabama (B.A. 2006) and its law school (J.D. 2010). The House bio says he grew up attending his grandfather's church.

profile.office_years_note: U.S. House since Jan 3, 2025 (about 1.75 years). Earlier White House and DOJ posts were appointed staff roles, not offices, and are not counted.

education.school: University of Alabama School of Law

career.role: Law clerk to Judge Nannette A. Baker
Domestic Director, Presidential Personnel Office; then White House liaison to AG Loretta Lynch
career.org: White House / U.S. Department of Justice

career.role: Legislative counsel to Sen. Sherrod Brown
Deputy chief of staff and counselor to AG Merrick Garland

platform.t: Backs Medicaid expansion in Alabama; sponsored the bipartisan Rural Hospital Stabilization Act (2025) and co-led the Bridge to Medicaid Act with Rep. Terri Sewell.
Introduced the Protecting American Beef Producers Act to void the Aug. 26, 2026 beef-import proclamation, and the Tariff Impacted Farmer Support Act (up to $15B for family farms).
Introduced the Affordable Youth Enrichment Opportunities Act (2026), a tax deduction for children's extracurricular costs.
Says the war with Iran is raising fuel and farm input costs. Voted Yea on H.Con.Res. 93 (Sep 15, 2026) directing removal of U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran.

promises.t: Stop the 2026 presidential beef-import order and require full tariffs on beef imports.
Win federal relief for farmers hurt by tariffs (Tariff Impacted Farmer Support Act).
Keep rural hospitals open through federal grant support (Rural Hospital Stabilization Act).

record.t: No itemized total was found. One documented item: $1 million in FY2026 appropriations for the Jackson (Clarke County) Health Care Authority. Congress.gov and House appropriations request lists were not reachable.

claims.claim: Marques voted for a 67% gas and diesel tax increase.

record.t: Marques did vote for the 2019 Rebuild Alabama fuel-tax increase (al.com via Wikipedia). The 67% figure was not checked against the act's rate schedule. The 67% figure itself was not independently checked against the 2019 law's per-gallon rates, so this claim is not rated.

claims.claim: Figures brought all sides together to keep Jackson Hospital open, which 'threatened care for 55,000.'

record.t: Reflector, 1819 News, WSFA and WTVM coverage of the Jackson–Blue Cross negotiation and the Aug. 17, 2026 deal names the CEO, Gov. Ivey, Mayor Reed, the county commission and Jackson Healthcare. None names Figures or mentions 55,000 patients. Any private role he played is not documented in those sources.

claims.claim: Is leading the effort to stop foreign beef imports undercutting farmers.

record.t: Introduced the Protecting American Beef Producers Act on Sep 2, 2026 to void Proclamation 11059. The release lists no cosponsors. Whether he 'leads' the wider effort is characterization.

claims.claim: Is pushing economic relief for farmers hurt by global tariffs.

record.t: Introduced the Tariff Impacted Farmer Support Act of 2026 (up to $15B in relief).

entries.t: Asked the DNC to adopt more crypto-friendly policy and urged a 'pro-innovation' SEC chair (APR, Jul 29, 2024, via Wikipedia).
Voted Yea on H.Con.Res. 93 War Powers resolution (Sep 15, 2026); criticizes the war's effect on fuel prices.

support: DCCC (coordinated TV ads with campaign, six-figure, 3 markets, Sep 2026)

fec.outside_note: 2026: no independent-expenditure totals found. National parties are 'pouring in millions' (ADN). The NRCC named AL-02 a priority but no amount was reported. FEC outside-spending tables did not load. 2024 (for context): Protect Progress (crypto super PAC) spent $1,723,976 (primary) + $668,419 (runoff) for him and $239,714 against Anthony Daniels. New Southern Majority IE PAC spent $87,812 for him. DMFI PAC, Rolling Sea Action Fund and 1000 Women Strong also spent for him, and Alabama Families PAC against him (amounts not shown).

corp.t: Corporate and trade PACs gave in 2024, including Regions Financial, Truist, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alabama, Ernst & Young, Volkert (DVAHC) PAC and National Beer Wholesalers ($5,000 each). In the 2024 primary and runoff, the crypto-industry super PAC Protect Progress spent about $2.39M supporting him. PAC money is about 63% of his 2025–26 contributions ($830,338 of $1,321,283).

lobby.t: Pro-Israel PAC money: AIPAC PAC gave $5,000 directly (Oct 2024) and DMFI PAC $1,000 (Sep 2024). DMFI PAC also made independent expenditures for him in 2024. Track AIPAC lists a $63,235 career pro-Israel total.

superpac_donors.note: Its funders were not documented in the sources reached. Direct crypto-linked contributions to his campaign: Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss $3,300 each, Coinbase Innovation PAC $1,000, Brian Armstrong $1,000.

research_notes: FEC: 2026 candidate page (through Jul 22, 2026) and 2024 committee page (Oct 1, 2023–Dec 31, 2024) read directly. The 2024 candidate page was rate-limited. Track AIPAC (data 7/5/26) lists him at $63,235 career. AL-02 race: Cook rates it Likely R, Sabato Leans R (moved Sep 10/11, 2026). A June Impact Research (D) poll had Marques 45, Figures 44, and a DCCC poll had 46–46. The 2024 PAC list from ProPublica is partial: sorted by date, cut off, and $2,500-and-under gifts not shown. The 'Iran war' referenced by both campaigns is described as ongoing in 2026 reporting; it was not independently researched here. The web-search budget ran out partway through.
